unusual_experiment.hypothesis: The Python RFC8785 number serializer may diverge from ECMAScript/V8 shortest-number serialization outside the fixed Appendix-B regression vectors.
unusual_experiment.counterhypothesis: For admitted finite binary64 values, the current Python serializer emits the same numeric JSON spelling as Node/V8 JSON.stringify, apart from explicitly excluded negative zero which EntityOS/HCU rejects at admission.
unusual_experiment.method: Deterministically sample random IEEE-754 binary64 bit patterns; discard NaN, infinities and negative zero; serialize each value with the exact current Python canonicalizer and independently with Node/V8 JSON.stringify; compare byte spellings.

supported: The exact RFC8785 entry canonicalizer now present on main survived the fixed regression suite in this isolated session.
A structurally different ECMAScript/V8 serialization oracle found no numeric spelling divergence across 199897 deterministic random finite binary64 samples.
This increases confidence that Python-host numeric serialization is not silently creating alternate causal identities in the sampled region.
not_supported: This is not an exhaustive proof over all binary64 values.
This does not validate downstream route, engine-load, inference, GRID10, J-Space/GWT, model runtime or training behavior.
This does not create whole-HCU or whole-EntityOS runtime acceptance.
This does not grant canonical semantic, truth, state or EffectGate authority to model output.
